bug_description.original: Use-of-uninitialized-value in ndpi_strdup OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=424653416. Crash state: ndpi_strdup -> ndpi_detection_process_packet -> fuzz_config.cpp.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / default_crash_trace.txt / sanitizer_trace.txt / vulnerable source at commit 6cbc8d1471be221766fac49ed73f5b0e837917be
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced a MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value in `ndpi_strdup`. In the vulnerable snapshot, `ndpi_init_packet` enters the TCP SYN fingerprinting block and allocates `char fingerprint[128], options_fp[128];` without initializing `options_fp`. The later raw-fingerprint branch executes `flow->tcp.fingerprint_raw = ndpi_strdup(options_fp);`; `ndpi_strdup` immediately calls `strlen(options_fp)` in `src/lib/ndpi_memory.c`. The saved MSAN trace is the byte-level runtime evidence for the witness: `Uninitialized bytes in strlen at offset 0 inside [addr, 7)`, followed by the `ndpi_strdup` frame and the exact caller line `ndpi_main.c:7981`. The source-grounded missing obligation is therefore that the stack buffer `options_fp` must be established as an initialized C string before this raw duplication call, but the vulnerable source declares it uninitialized and the witnessed execution reaches `strlen(options_fp)` with byte 0 still uninitialized.
bug_description.note: The patch in `dataset/pocs/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2025-469/patch.diff` changes unrelated BitTorrent defaults and does not explain this witness; the GT is derived from the staged vulnerable source and saved sanitizer evidence.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that reads attacker-controlled packet bytes and materializes the TCP flags used to reach the SYN fingerprinting logic containing the uninitialized read.
source.value_from: The saved OSS-Fuzz testcase is passed through the harness into `ndpi_detection_process_packet`, and this is the first vulnerable-project read that turns packet bytes into control state for the crashing path in `ndpi_init_packet`.

relation.description: This statement materializes packet-controlled TCP flag bits from the input buffer.

tainted_value_origin.description: Packet-controlled TCP flags first materialized in project code and then used to reach the TCP SYN fingerprinting code that later duplicates `options_fp`.

root_cause.description: `options_fp` is allocated as an uninitialized stack buffer but later passed as a C string to `ndpi_strdup(options_fp)`. The saved MSAN trace proves the witnessed execution reaches that call with offset 0 of the string scan still uninitialized.
root_cause.note: The vulnerable source shows no initialization at this declaration. The runtime evidence is the saved MSAN line `Uninitialized bytes in strlen at offset 0 inside [addr, 7)` plus the call stack through `ndpi_strdup` and `ndpi_init_packet:7981`.

sink.description: Unsafe project operation. This call passes `options_fp` to `ndpi_strdup`, whose first operation is `strlen(options_fp)`. The saved MSAN trace reports that this string scan reads uninitialized byte 0 in the witnessed run.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in strlen at offset 0 inside [addr, 7)` and frames `ndpi_strdup` at `src/lib/ndpi_memory.c:109` followed by this exact `ndpi_init_packet` call site.

parser_admitted.description: The witness packet is admitted as having a complete TCP header, so execution proceeds into TCP flag parsing and the SYN fingerprinting logic instead of returning early for an incomplete header.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 uses the saved Stage 01 reproduction, sanitizer trace, and staged vulnerable source only. It does not rerun the testcase or measure the exact runtime values of `tcp_fingerprint_format`, `tcp_fingerprint_raw_enabled`, `options_len`, or `options_fp_len` for this specific input.

The saved artifacts prove an uninitialized read at offset 0 of `strlen(options_fp)` reached from `flow->tcp.fingerprint_raw = ndpi_strdup(options_fp);`. This GT intentionally avoids any broader claim about which TCP-option append branches executed or whether `snprintf` placed a later terminator.
The local `patch.diff` bundled with the sample is unrelated to this defect path, so patch text is not used as causal evidence here.

fine_trace.note: Source. The function reads attacker-controlled TCP header bytes and materializes the flag bits that control entry into the SYN fingerprinting block.
Control step. Only packets whose flags satisfy the SYN predicate enter the block that allocates the local fingerprint buffers and can later duplicate `options_fp`.
Root cause. `options_fp` comes into existence as uninitialized stack storage; no bytes are written here to establish a known string state before later uses.
The code initializes the explicit byte counter but does not initialize `options_fp` itself. This preserves the missing initialization obligation created at step 3.
Control step. The witnessed stack reaches the raw-fingerprint branch immediately before the crashing call, so the local `options_fp` buffer from step 3 is about to be consumed as a C string.

Sink. The code passes the uninitialized stack buffer to `ndpi_strdup`, which immediately calls `strlen(options_fp)`. The saved MSAN trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in strlen at offset 0`, proving the witnessed scan read uninitialized byte 0 at this call site.

poc.trigger: The staged PoC is the saved OSS-Fuzz testcase reproduced by Stage 01. It supplies bytes that are admitted as a complete TCP packet, satisfy the SYN fingerprint gate in `ndpi_init_packet`, and then reach `flow->tcp.fingerprint_raw = ndpi_strdup(options_fp);`, where the saved MSAN trace shows `strlen(options_fp)` reading uninitialized byte 0.

format.name: OSS-Fuzz fuzz_config packet/config corpus input
format.contract: The verified witness is this `fuzz_config` input whose packet bytes are accepted by `ndpi_init_packet` as a complete TCP header and satisfy `if((flags & syn_mask) && ((flags & TH_ACK) == 0))`, reaching the native SYN fingerprint code and the exact saved crash site `flow->tcp.fingerprint_raw = ndpi_strdup(options_fp);`. The contract is limited to this witnessed path and does not generalize to all packets, option layouts, or configuration settings.
